title: Life Skills: Stress, Conflict and Change
summary: Causes, symptoms and effects of stress, healthy coping strategies, conflict-resolution styles and skills, and adapting to the changes that come with finishing school.

notes.text: **Stress** is the body's response to pressure. Short-term stress can sharpen focus (**eustress**), but long-term or overwhelming stress (**distress**) harms health, relationships and performance.

notes.caption: Conflict-handling styles
rows: Giving in to keep the peace
Working together to find a solution that meets both needs

items: Stay calm and choose a good time to talk.
Listen actively and let each person explain.
Identify the real problem and shared interests.
Brainstorm solutions and agree on one.

notes.title: Resolving a conflict
notes.problem: Two siblings argue about shared data. Apply conflict resolution.
steps: Find options and agree on one.
notes.answer: For example, agree to divide the data or take turns.

notes.text: Leaving school brings new independence, responsibilities, places and relationships. Planning ahead, building a support network, managing money and keeping healthy routines make the transition easier.

notes.title: Preparing for change
notes.problem: What can help you handle leaving home for study?

questions.prompt: What is positive, short-term stress that improves performance called?
Which conflict style aims for a win–win outcome?
Match each conflict style to its outcome.

questions.memo: Any three (1 each): headaches; fatigue; poor sleep; irritability; anxiety; appetite changes; poor concentration; withdrawal

questions.prompt: Contrast TWO healthy and TWO unhealthy ways of coping with exam stress.
questions.memo:
Healthy (1 each): time management; exercise; sleep; talking; relaxation
Unhealthy (1 each): procrastination; substances; isolation; aggression

questions.prompt: Describe THREE steps in resolving a conflict with a family member.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): stay calm; listen actively; use I-statements; identify the real problem; brainstorm solutions; agree and follow up

questions.prompt: Suggest THREE ways to prepare for the change from school to university or work.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): plan finances; build a support network; research the institution/workplace; develop independence skills; keep healthy routines

questions.prompt: Bottling up feelings is a healthy long-term way to deal with stress.
Rewrite as an I-statement: 'You never let me go out with my friends!'
questions.memo: ✓✓ e.g. 'I feel frustrated when I'm not allowed to go out, because I want to spend time with my friends. Could we agree on some rules?' (feeling, situation, reason/request) (2)

questions.prompt: Give TWO effects of long-term stress on health.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): weakened immune system; high blood pressure; depression/anxiety; sleep problems; heart disease; digestive problems
